author: Staff Writer
title: UPDATE: Police arrest suspect in deadly Wilmington Hospital shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Writer ,
6 hours ago One ChristianaCare employee was killed and another critically wounded in what officials called a targeted attack WILMINGTON — Police have arrested the man they say shot two ChristianaCare employees inside Wilmington Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, killing one and critically wounding another.
Wilmington Police identified the suspect as John Wallace-Bey, 23, of New Castle. Police said Wallace-Bey was arrested late Tuesday night in Philadelphia after a manhunt that followed the shooting, which happened shortly after 3:30 p.m. on June 16.
Pending extradition to Delaware, Wallace-Bey is expected to face charges of murder and attempted murder, police said.
ChristianaCare said Wallace-Bey and both victims were employees of the health system. Both victims were 19 years old. One was pronounced dead, and the second was listed in critical but stable condition. Their identities had not been released as of Wednesday.
Wilmington Police Chief Wilfredo Campos said investigators were still working to determine key details, including where inside the hospital the shooting occurred, how Wallace-Bey was able to leave the building and how a gun was brought into the hospital.
Campos said license plate-reading technology helped investigators locate the suspect.
The shooting prompted a major law enforcement response and a lockdown at the Wilmington campus Tuesday afternoon. The campus reopened Wednesday with normal operations.
Mayor John Carney said Wednesday that the shooting was especially painful because it took place inside a facility dedicated to saving lives.
“I’m heartbroken for the victims and their loved ones, for the ChristianaCare team, and for the entire city of Wilmington,” Carney said. “Violence has no place in our community. It’s particularly distressing that such violence and tragedy unfolded at a facility with a primary function of providing lifesaving care. Our health care workers and their patients should never fear for their safety.”
Carney also praised police and first responders.
“While others run away from danger, our law enforcement officers and first responders run toward it,” Carney said. “The Wilmington Police Department and partner agencies handled this tragedy with bravery and professionalism, and we owe them a debt of gratitude for their service to our community.”
Campos said the department’s Victim Services Unit continues to assist the victims’ families and the ChristianaCare community.
“Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with the victims and their families, as well as the ChristianaCare community,” Campos said. “Our Victim Services Unit continues to provide assistance during this difficult time, and we stand at the ready to support our partners at ChristianaCare in the days and weeks to come.”
Campos also thanked Wilmington officers and the local, state and federal agencies that assisted, including Delaware State Police, New Castle County Police, New Castle City Police, Delaware Probation and Parole, DNREC Police, the FBI, ATF, Wilmington Fire Department, New Castle County Paramedics and several area fire companies.
“I would like to thank all of the Wilmington Police officers who responded to yesterday’s tragic incident,” Campos said. “Day in and day out, these brave police officers run toward danger to protect and serve our community, and their response yesterday was no different.”
The investigation remains ongoing.

Police said Wallace-Bey was arrested late Tuesday night in Philadelphia after a manhunt that followed the shooting, which happened shortly after 3:30 p.m. on June 16. The shooting prompted a major law enforcement response and a lockdown at the Wilmington campus Tuesday afternoon.
